source.quote: Shanling's own manual for the SM50, read 2026-11-25; its product page /product/505 is image-only. Its single rate figure sits under the manual's own heading « USB Driver Playback »: « Support up to PCM 768kHz and DSD512. » The SM50's manual additionally gives « Input Options: "Streaming | BT Input | USB IN" » and « Output Options: "Pre-Out | Line-Out | Headphone | COAXIAL | USB OUT" », and its « USB IN Mode » section carries NO figure; its settings include a « Filter » item whose options are not printed. No converter part number is given.

_la_source_est_une_annonce_ou_un_manuel_: Shanling's product pages are image-only, so every figure comes from the maker's own announcement at /article/NNNNNN or from its manual PDF, both on en.shanling.com. No number was read off an image, and nothing is sourced to store.shanling.com. See the brand file.
_ni_DoP_ni_natif_ne_sont_dits_pour_ce_mo: DoP appears on no Shanling page or manual, and « native » only in the UA dongle manuals and in EM5. Neither is stated for this model.
_le_chiffre_est_sous_le_titre_LECTURE_DE: « Support up to PCM 768kHz and DSD512 » appears under « USB Driver Playback » - reading files off a stick - and the section describing the USB INPUT has no figure at all. All three SM network players do this identically. So `pcm_max_hz` and `dsd_max` record what the device converts when it plays a file, `inputs` is empty, and a reader wanting to know what these streamers accept from a computer will not find it on this maker's site. The same shape as the EH3 and the EC3, three times over.
_le_COAXIAL_est_dans_la_liste_des_SORTIE: « Output Options: "Pre-Out | Line-Out | Headphone | COAXIAL | USB OUT" » against « Input Options: "Streaming | BT Input | USB IN" ». Coaxial belongs to the outputs and USB appears on both sides. Fourth Shanling device where the word coaxial names an output, after the EC Zero T, the EC3 and the M1 Plus.
